person: Walt Brenner, 66, runs a 24-person surveying and renovation firm with crews in three states. He does his own HR with a part-time bookkeeper, and his new CPA firm's emails go unread. This fall he hired nine people for the busy season, and his bookkeeper mentioned a hiring tax credit he has never claimed. He prints everything, is wary of anything that sounds like a sales pitch, and wants to know what a missed deadline costs him.
stated_up_front: My bookkeeper says there's some tax credit for new hires and I've got nine this fall. I'm not a computer person. Tell me which ones qualify and what happens if we miss the date.

facts.about: Number of fall hires to screen
facts.truth: Nine hires between 29 September and 14 October.

facts.about: A laborer in a SNAP household
facts.truth: Dale Pruitt, age 31, began work 6 October, his SNAP award letter came in the mail, and the form was signed on the offer day, 2 October.

facts.about: A hire whose 28 days have run out
facts.truth: A survey rodman began 29 September; his 28th day was 26 October, and Walt wants him checked first.
Walt's wife's nephew, Kyle, started on a renovation crew; he is family, so no credit.
A carpenter, Hector Ruiz, worked for the firm two summers ago and was brought back in October.
Tom Alvarez left the Army 5 weeks before the offer, has no disability rating, and is out of work only a short time.

facts.about: Hire who answered no to all screening questions
facts.truth: A crew helper, Brian Osei, answered no to every question on the form.
An ex-felon release paper came for a laborer, but his form was signed 11 October, four days after his 7 October offer.
A surveyor tech accepted the offer on 3 October and then took a job elsewhere, never showing up.
The benefit and release letters sit in a manila folder on his desk, and the EIN is on his payroll stub.

unknowns: How many days the state allows after a start date, and what the cutoff is
Which target group each letter counts for, and what the group is worth
Whether the nephew being his wife's side counts as a relative under the rule
What the state's group codes mean or the maximum credit for each
